In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of receptor polymorphism in the host range variation of gammaretrovirues has not yet been fully elucidated.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dCAT-1 receptor variant of M. dunii cells is responsible for the unusual host range of the cytopathic ecotropic MLVs, and that the unusual glycosylation of this receptor may be a factor in the unusual host range and cytopathicity of these viruses.

the receptor polymorphism dCAT-1 is a key factor in the cytopathic phenotype of ecotropic MLVs in cells of M. dunui origin, and that glycosylation of the receptor may play a role in the host range variation of these viruses.

virus entry and syncytium formation are determined by the interaction of a few critical amino acid residues between virus and receptor, and that this interaction is modulated by cell-specific glycosylations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a few amino acid differences in a virus and/or a host cell can result in a dramatic difference in virus pathogenesis.
the host range of ecotropic gammaretrovirues is determined by the interaction of virus Env and cell receptor, which is modulated by receptor glycosylation.
receptor glycosylation may be a key determinant of virus entry and cytopathicity in cells of different species.
